title: edit-ideas-from-webui
description: I want to be able to edit an idea's description from the webui.

history.note:
Verdict: FAIL — Step ordering issue: Step 4 (state.py helper) should come BEFORE Step 3 (TUI handler), since Step 3 depends on the helper method. Move Step 4 to be Step 2.
Missing error handling: No handling for WebSocket send failures, Python save errors, or network issues. Plan should specify error responses.
Missing validation: No validation for description content (max length, empty allowed?, sanitization).
Feature not found: Step 1 doesn't specify what happens if featureID doesn't exist - should return 404 error.
Missing loading state: Web UI edit flow doesn't show loading state while saving or handle save failures with user feedback.
No callback return value: Step 2 doesn't specify how the Python handler should signal success/failure back to Go server for proper error reporting to user.

Feedback: Step ordering issue: Step 4 (state.py helper) should come BEFORE Step 3 (TUI handler), since Step 3 depends on the helper method. Move Step 4 to be Step 2.

Feature not found: Step 1 doesn't specify what happens if featureID doesn't exist - should return 404 error.

No callback return value: Step 2 doesn't specify how the Python handler should signal success/failure back to Go server for proper error reporting to user.

Feedback: Found several issues:

Step 3 (tui.py): Uses send_state(...) but the actual method is push_state(...) with signature push_state(features, plan_status, impl_status, auto_plan_enabled=..., auto_impl_enabled=...). The plan must use the correct method name and include all required arguments (see lines 1474-1478 in tui.py).

Step 5 (index.html): References function showFeatureDetail but the actual function is showFeature(card) at line 502.

Step 5 (index.html): Assumes _modalClientId and _modalFeatureId module-level variables exist, but they don't. The plan needs to add code to store these when showFeature() is called (extracting from card.getAttribute('data-id') and card.getAttribute('data-client')).

Step 2 (server_client.py): The callback signature should match existing patterns. Looking at on_idea_created (line 51), callbacks are stored and called with positional args, not keyword args.
